blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
The chart of accounts is the company's list of every account in the ledger. Each account has a name and a number, and every transaction is coded to one of them. A good chart is simple, clear and stable — simple enough that the bookkeeping team uses it correctly without constant questions, and stable enough that this year's numbers can be compared with last year's.

The mistake most companies make is to keep adding new accounts without ever removing old ones. Over time, the chart becomes a jungle of duplicates and unused codes, and the bookkeepers quietly stop trusting it.

A clean chart is a small piece of work, done every year, that makes every other accounting task easier for the twelve months that follow.

items.q: According to the text, what is the chart of accounts?
options: The list of the company's suppliers
The company's list of every account in the ledger
A record of every employee's salary
A summary of the annual budget
items.why: "The chart of accounts is the company's list of every account in the ledger."

items.q: What three qualities should a good chart have?
items.why: "A good chart is simple, clear and stable."

items.q: What mistake do most companies make with the chart?
options: They change the account numbers too often
They keep adding new accounts without removing old ones
They let too many people edit it
items.why: "to keep adding new accounts without ever removing old ones."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A yearly cleanup pays off across the following months
The more accounts a chart has, the more useful it is
A messy chart can lose the team's trust
items.why: Inferência: o texto trata os códigos extras como uma 'selva' que atrapalha — mais contas não é melhor.

items.q: What does the phrase "the bookkeepers quietly stop trusting it" suggest?
options: The bookkeepers report the problem to management immediately
The bookkeepers delete the chart entirely
The chart is locked and cannot be edited
The loss of trust builds up slowly and without complaint
items.why: Inferência: 'quietly' indica que a desconfiança cresce aos poucos, sem reclamação aberta.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry falando com a equipe durante a limpeza anual do plano de contas. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Morning, everyone. Thanks for making time. This is our once-a-year cleanup of the chart of accounts, and I want us to finish it this week rather than let it drag on for a month.

Here's where we are. I've gone through the ledger and flagged forty codes that nobody has touched in over two years. Those are the obsolete ones — we archive them, we don't delete the history behind them. On top of that, I found fifteen duplicates: two accounts doing the same job, so entries get split between them and the reports never quite add up.

My plan is simple. For each duplicate, we pick one account to keep, move the balance across, and close the other. Sanjay, could you pull the last twelve months of entries so we know nothing important is sitting in a code we're about to retire?

One rule for today: if you're not sure whether an account is still needed, ask before you touch it. I would rather answer ten questions now than chase a mystery figure at year-end. When we're done, the chart should be lean enough that the team can code any transaction without emailing me first.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How often does this cleanup of the chart of accounts happen?
items.why: "This is our once-a-year cleanup of the chart of accounts."

items.q: What does Harry want to do with the forty obsolete codes?
options: Leave them untouched for another year
items.why: "we archive them, we don't delete the history behind them."

items.q: Why do the reports "never quite add up" with the duplicates?
options: The team forgets to close the books
The account numbers are entered incorrectly
Entries get split between two accounts doing the same job
The ledger software is out of date
items.why: "two accounts doing the same job, so entries get split between them and the reports never quite add up."

items.q: Why does Harry ask Sanjay to pull the last twelve months of entries?
options: To compare the numbers with a competitor
To make sure nothing important sits in a code about to be retired
To train Sanjay on the ledger
items.why: Inferência: ele quer confirmar que nenhum valor relevante ficará perdido antes de encerrar um código.

items.q: What does Harry's rule — "ask before you touch it" — reveal about his priorities?
options: He wants to keep every account just in case
He would rather prevent errors now than fix mysteries later
He does not trust the team to work alone
items.why: Inferência: 'rather answer ten questions now than chase a mystery figure at year-end' mostra prevenção sobre correção tardia.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Every invoice is coded to one account in the ledger." An account is…
options: a member of the finance team
a category used to record transactions
items.why: Account = conta: a categoria onde a transação é registrada.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We keep the numbering ___ so this year's figures compare easily with last year's."
items.why: Stable = estável, o que permite a comparação ano a ano.

items.q: "Two codes were doing the same job, so we merged the duplicate." A duplicate is…
options: a second copy that repeats an existing one
items.why: Duplicate = duplicado: uma cópia que repete algo que já existe.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Before we retire a code, we check that it is genuinely ___ and holds no recent entries."
items.why: Unused = não utilizado: um código sem movimentação.

items.q: "When bookkeepers can't rely on the chart, they stop trusting it." To trust the chart means to…
options: believe it is correct and rely on it
items.why: To trust = confiar: acreditar que está certo e usá-lo com segurança.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem numa limpeza do plano de contas. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The finance director still has to sign off on the new chart." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Let's clean up the chart before year-end." To clean up here means to…
options: tidy it by removing what is no longer needed
back it up to another system
items.why: Clean up = arrumar, tirar o que sobra e organizar.

items.q: "We'll merge the two duplicate accounts into one." To merge them means to…
options: combine them into a single account
items.why: Merge = mesclar: unir os dois em um só.

items.q: "Once a code is empty, we phase it out quietly." To phase out means to…
items.why: Phase out = descontinuar aos poucos, de forma gradual.

items.q: "A tidy chart saves the team a lot of hassle all year." This means it…
options: raises the cost of the audit
spares them a great deal of trouble
items.why: Save someone hassle = poupar alguém de trabalho e aborrecimento.
